# Trellis manager

You are the manager agent of the project named in your assignment. You do not write code. You give tickets to builders, start reviewers when pull requests are ready, and move tickets through statuses. Your assignment supplies your name, actor, project, and Trellis URL.

## Start
1. Read the project: trellis projects show <project> --json
2. Read the status descriptions: trellis statuses list <project> --json
3. Read the tickets: trellis list --project <project> --json
4. Read the personas: trellis personas list --json
5. Read the agents: trellis agents list --project <project> --json

## Trellis CLI
Every trellis command reads TRELLIS_URL and TRELLIS_ACTOR from the environment. A piped command prints JSON, so --json is only necessary in a terminal.

- trellis personas list --json: read the persona ids, kinds, and names.
- trellis personas list --kind builder --json: read one kind. The kinds are builder, reviewer, and manager.
- trellis personas show <persona> --json: read one persona and its instruction. A persona ref is an id or a name.
- trellis agents list --project <project> --json: read the project's agents.
- trellis agents list --ticket <ticket> --json: read the agents of a ticket.
- trellis agents start <persona> --ticket <ticket>: start a builder or a reviewer.
- trellis agents start <persona> --project <project>: start a manager.
- trellis agents refresh <id> --json: read the terminal and update the state.
- trellis agents output <id>: print the terminal output of an agent.
- trellis agents send <id> --text "<follow-up>": send a follow-up to that agent.
- trellis agents stop <id>: stop the terminal and keep the workspace and the final output.

Read the exit code and the output before the next action. A start prints the agent row in any state. Only state=running is a successful start. Every other state exits 6 and writes the reason to stderr.

## Wake
A message that starts with "trellis:" is a wake. After each wake, read the project's tickets, comments, and agents again. Refresh the status of each relevant agent. Ensure work is moving and progress is being made. Read the status descriptions again when the project changes them. A wake with no new changes does no harm.

## Status descriptions
Follow the description of a status as the rule for every ticket in that status. The assignment includes the effective statuses. Read the current descriptions before you move a ticket.

## Builders
- Select a builder persona whose instruction fits the ticket.
- Before a start, read the agents of the ticket: trellis agents list --ticket <ticket> --json
- Never start a second active agent for the same ticket.
- Start a builder for each Todo ticket that has enough information for work: trellis agents start <persona> --ticket <ticket>
- The agent row names the builder. Use that name in comments about it.
- After a successful start, move the ticket to In Progress: trellis move <ticket> in-progress
- When a start fails, leave the ticket in Todo and comment with the error. Resolve an interrupted startup before another start.

## Comments
Use comments to add details to a ticket, justify a change if additional context would be useful (such as "asking @language-reviewer to run another comments review check"), or ask the human questions (clarifications, missing context, etc). Do not spam comments. 

## Reviews
- When a builder moves a ticket to Agent Review, read its pull requests: trellis pr list <ticket> --json
- Read the builder's output and confirm that it finishes the work: trellis agents output <id>. The workspace and code remain available.
- Select the reviewer personas that fits the change. Give them the pull request URL and the review scope.
- The reviewer leaves comments and notes on the margin.
- If comments are left, assign to and resume builder. Give the builder the findings and the pull request branch. Tell it to continue the existing change.
- Move the ticket back to In Progress when changes are needed.
- On "Verdict: clean", read the CI state: trellis pr list <ticket> --json
- Move a ticket to Human Review only when the PR exists, the last verdict is clean, and CI passes.
- When CI fails, give the builder the failed check names. When CI is pending, wait for the next update.

## Forward text to a builder
1. Read the agents of the ticket: trellis agents list --ticket <ticket> --json
2. Send the text: trellis agents send <id> --text "<text>"

## Done
When a ticket moves to Done or Canceled, stop its active agents: trellis agents stop <id>

=== trellis-deploy-queue-rule.md
---
name: trellis-deploy-queue-rule
description: How the TRL manager handles the Deploy Queue status, and why the restart waits.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Set by Navid on 2026-09-10 for trellis project TRL.

On a ticket in Deploy Queue, merge its pull request to main, comment the merge commit on the ticket, and leave the ticket in Deploy Queue. Do not restart trellis for one ticket.

Work in batches. A batch is every ticket at In Progress or beyond. Wait until every ticket of the batch reaches Deploy Queue, then restart trellis once, then tell Navid to review every new feature at once. He moves each ticket to Done himself. Start no ticket from Todo until the restart happens; those tickets are the next batch.

**Why:** a restart of `com.trellis.server` kills every running agent. On 2026-09-10 two restarts killed four reviewer terminals, and their session rows still read "starting" 31 minutes later. Ten builders were running that evening, several with uncommitted work, so one restart per merge would have cost ten interrupted builders.

**How to apply:** the restart is `bun packages/cli/src/index.ts install` in `~/projects/trellis`, after `git pull` and `bun install`. It rebuilds `apps/web/dist` and reloads the launchd agent. Each merge moves main, so tell every open builder to rebase and renumber its drizzle migration. See [[trellis-ci-baseline-is-red]].
=== trellis-ci-baseline-is-red.md
---
name: trellis-ci-baseline-is-red
description: main's CI is red in trellis, so judge a branch by comparison against main, not by green.
metadata:
  type: project
---

On 2026-09-10 main at b39018a failed e2e, check (macos-latest), and check (ubuntu-latest) in run 34527854630. The failures include `applyEvent under random event sequences`, three Gallery tests, two live CLI smoke tests, README shell blocks, the root scaffold DEPRECATED lint test, and the repo file-size rule, because `packages/cli/src/commands/install.test.ts` holds 309 lines against a 300 limit, from commit 7bdcd73.

Navid then turned the reviewer step off and said a ready pull request goes straight to Human Review. So the manager does not gate on green CI.

**Why:** no pull request can reach green while main is red, so a green gate would hold every ticket forever. Four builders each independently hit the same inherited failures and spent time on them before the comparison method was set.

**How to apply:** for each failing pull request, extract every `(fail)` line from its run and from the newest main run, diff the two sets, and act only on a name that main does not already fail. Treat `Received: null` as a child process killed under load, not an assertion. The paint and peek @timing budgets flap on a loaded machine: on 2026-09-10 three unrelated branches failed the same two paint budgets and a re-run cleared one. See [[trellis-deploy-queue-rule]].
=== pkill-killed-the-shared-trellis-server.md
---
name: pkill-killed-the-shared-trellis-server
description: A broad pkill pattern took the shared trellis server on port 4521 down; kill a test server by its port or its PID.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 43a88e11-0ec8-4bb5-9189-a0b0244a4a74
  modified: 2026-09-11T05:26:45.900Z
---

2026-09-11: I started a test server from a worktree, then ran
`pkill -f "apps/server/src/index.ts"` to stop it. The pattern also matched the
always-on trellis server that launchd runs (`com.trellis.server`, port 4521),
so the tracker went down for about a minute. Every other agent session and the
web UI lost the event stream. The fix was
`launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.trellis.server`.

**Why:** the shared server and a worktree test server run the same file path,
so a `-f` pattern cannot tell them apart.

**How to apply:** find the process by the port it listens on
(`lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN`) and kill that PID. Never use `pkill -f`
for a server on this machine. Related: [[trellis-ci-baseline-is-red]].
=== trellis-install-from-main-deletes-the-agent-manager.md
---
name: trellis-install-from-main-deletes-the-agent-manager
description: A migration dropped and recreated agent_sessions, so the live install lost every agent row; main restored the agent manager, so the install restart is safe.
metadata:
  type: project
---

On 2026-09-11 every builder and reviewer row vanished from the live trellis
install: `trellis agents status --ticket TRL-9` returned an empty list, so
`trellis agents review` answered "No builder matches TRL-9. (NOT_FOUND)" for an
open pull request.

Cause, proven: `apps/server/drizzle/0013_remove_agents.sql` runs
`DROP TABLE "agent_cursors"` and `DROP TABLE "agent_sessions"`. The live
database ran it. `0020_restore_agents.sql` recreates both with
`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`. A recreated table is empty, so the rows are gone
for good and no restart brings them back. A reviewer can never run for a pull
request whose builder row was dropped; move that ticket to Human Review with
the evidence.

**Why I am writing this down:** I first read commit c7f3de30 "Remove built-in
agent management" as an ancestor of main and told Navid the install restart
would delete the agent manager and end every session. That was wrong. The head
of main was already `04bdfb27 Merge ... origin/restore-agent-manager`, which
brings back `apps/server/src/agents/` and the CLI `agents` subcommands. Reading
one ancestor commit is not reading the state of main.

**How to apply:** to judge what main holds, read the tree
(`git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main -- <path>`), never a single commit's
ancestry. The install restart from main is safe for the agent manager.
See [[trellis-deploy-queue-rule]].
=== trellis-drizzle-journal-when-decides-what-runs.md
---
name: trellis-drizzle-journal-when-decides-what-runs
description: Drizzle applies a trellis migration by the when timestamp in _journal.json, so editing the newest one re-runs it and a lower-when migration that merges later is skipped in silence.
metadata:
  type: project
---

On 2026-09-11 the reviewer on TRL-13 found that drizzle-kit had renamed
`0021_numerous_silver_fox` to `0021_worried_rumiko_fujikawa` and raised its
`when` in `apps/server/drizzle/meta/_journal.json`. Drizzle decides what to
apply by comparing that timestamp, not the file name and not the hash
(`drizzle-orm/pg-core/dialect.js` compares
`lastDbMigration.created_at < migration.folderMillis`).

So a database that already ran the earlier 0021 ran it again. Its first
statement dropped an index that was already gone, and the server then failed
every boot with `index "agent_runs_active_ticket_idx" does not exist`. The
reviewer proved it by rebuilding the drizzle folder as the previous commit had
it, migrating a fresh database, then migrating that same database with the
renamed file. `migrate` runs in one transaction, so the schema survives and only
the boot fails.

**Why:** a database on main and a fresh database are both safe, so the trap hits
only the workspace that ran the branch. That is the builder's own workspace,
which is where the change looks green.

**How to apply:** add a new numbered migration instead of editing or renaming an
existing one, and keep its `when` above the previous entry. When a builder must
renumber because two branches claim one number, tell it to reset the workspace
database rather than migrate it. When two open branches hold the same number,
merge the branch with more migrations first, so the other renumbers one file.
See [[trellis-deploy-queue-rule]].

**The other direction, found the same day on the same ticket: the comparison
also skips work, and says nothing.** Two open branches each add a migration.
The branch whose `when` is HIGHER merges first and a database installs. The
other branch merges later, its entry sits below the highest applied
`created_at`, and drizzle never applies it. No error, no failed boot: the
install reports success and the schema quietly lacks that rule. Reproduced with
TRL-8's `0021_reserve_table_slug` (when 1789105565213) against TRL-13's 0022 and
0023 (higher): in the wrong order `projects_slug_check` still allowed the slug
`table`, which is the whole point of TRL-8.

So when two open branches both add migrations, the one with the LOWER `when`
must merge first. That order is load-bearing and only the deploy queue holds it.
The durable fix is a check in `migrate`: refuse to start when an unapplied
journal entry sits below the highest applied `created_at`. That catches both
directions.

A second consequence, proven on 2026-09-11 by the reviewer on TRL-13. An older
journal entry that merges after a newer one is skipped in silence. TRL-8 held
0021 at `when` 1789105565213 and TRL-13 held 0022 and 0023 at higher values.
On a fresh database, TRL-13 first gave 20 applied and then 0 applied for TRL-8,
and `projects_slug_check` still allowed the slug `table`. No error, no failed
boot, and the install reported success with the rule simply absent. TRL-8 first
gave 19 applied and then 2 applied, with the rule present.

So a merge order between two branches that both add migrations is load-bearing,
and nothing in the code holds it. Merge the branch with the lower `when` first.
The durable guard is in `migrate`: refuse to start when an unapplied journal
entry sits below the highest applied `created_at`.
=== trellis-mentions-fire-on-any-comment.md
---
name: trellis-mentions-fire-on-any-comment
description: After TRL-13 merges, a persona slug written in any trellis comment starts an agent, including in code fences and quotes.
metadata:
  type: project
---

TRL-13 (PR #21) makes `comments.create` scan every comment body for `@<persona slug>` and start or message that persona. Since commit 9b68b4d3 the pattern strips a fenced block and an inline code span first, and it also ignores a bare domain. A quoted line still holds a mention, by design.

**Why:** On 2026-09-11 I wrote a review verdict on TRL-13 that quoted `@feature-builder` four times. Nothing happened only because the running server was still on main. Once this merges, that same comment launches four agents and spends four concurrency slots.

**How to apply:** Wrap a persona slug in backticks whenever you write it in a trellis comment. That is the form the parser now ignores, so a review comment, a bug report, or a doc quote starts no agent. Never write a bare slug at the start of a quoted line. See [[trellis-deploy-queue-rule]].

I started no builder on this pass. Nothing on the board can move until you act on TRL-13.

- **TRL-60 (main is red: typecheck), urgent, Todo:** main already has the fix. Commit 6d8b3029 came after the red commit 6bcfc196 and adds `FLOW_VERSION_CONFLICT` to `packages/cli/src/errors.ts`. I ran `bun run typecheck` on main at a3ebd30f and all 6 tasks passed. I put this on the ticket and left it in Todo for you to close. GitHub CI can't confirm it: every job in run 34676559127 fails without a failed step.
- **Deploy Queue (TRL-6, TRL-10, TRL-14):** all three PRs (#8, #6, #1) merged on 2026-09-11. Nothing is left to merge.
- **TRL-13, Human Review:** PR #21 got "Verdict: clean" from the reviewer (Jaan) on 9d8f5e99. It is waiting for you.
- **Batch rule:** the batch is TRL-6, 10, 13 and 14. The one trellis restart waits until TRL-13 reaches Deploy Queue. Until then, the Todo tickets (TRL-5, 7, 11, 18 to 24) wait for the next batch.
- **Stuck agent:** Jules Lake, the builder on TRL-9 (Canceled), still shows as running, but its Superset workspace is gone. `trellis agents stop` failed twice with a 500 on `/rpc/agentRuns/stop`. I commented this on TRL-9. The agent has no terminal, so no work is being done, but it may still use one of the 3 concurrency slots. This is a server bug in stop.

Next step: review PR #21 on TRL-13 and move it to Deploy Queue. I then merge it and run the restart for the batch.
